paper_metadata.title: Strengthening at high temperatures by precipitates in FeAlNb alloys

evidence.quote: Strengthening at high temperatures by precipitates in FeeAleNb alloys

Results are presented here on a variety of Fe eAleNb al-loys prepared by induction melting and drop casting into cyl-inders of 20 e30 mm in diameter. Al contents between 15% and 30% were examined (atomic percent is given throughout). A Nb content of 5% was initially used (for the alloy with 20% Al), but it was seen that the solid state solubility of Nb in these alloys was much less, even at very high temperatures, and hence subsequent alloys were prepared with the Nb content re-duced to 2%.

evidence.section: 3.1. Mechanical testing of Fe e25Ale2Nb at high temperatures
evidence.quote: This material was tested both in the solutionised state (after an anneal of 1 h at 1300 /C14 C, followed by a water quench) and in the precipitated state, after a further anneal of 1 h at 900 /C14 C.

evidence.section: 3.1. Mechanical testing of Fe e25Ale2Nb at high temperatures
evidence.quote: Fig. 1 shows that the present Fe e25Ale2Nb alloy has good strength from room temper-ature to about 500 /C14 C, due to solution and precipitate hard-ening, but that the flow stress falls rapidly thereafter to very low values for test temperatures of 700 e800 /C14 C and above.
